headline: Nvidia's encrypted firmware tanks Linux inference speed to 35 percent
body: Nvidia's RTX Spark encrypted firmware is delivering a significant performance hit on Linux systems, reducing inference speed to just 35 percent of baseline capacity. For healthcare AI vendors deploying clinical decision support, imaging analysis, or real-time patient monitoring on Linux infrastructure, this creates a critical bottleneck that undermines the cost-benefit case for GPU acceleration. Combined with rising hardware costs and Nvidia's pivot toward subscription-based licensing models, healthcare organizations face mounting pressure to either absorb performance penalties or renegotiate deployment architectures. This matters for EHR-integrated AI workloads and value-based care analytics that depend on predictable, high-throughput inference to justify infrastructure investments.
